Two holes in the floor battery, both found by running the arming pre-check
diag_refuses' own licence prescribes.

run-micro.sh counted diagnostics with grep -c '^[EW]_', anchored at line
start. Every diagnostic is phase-prefixed — "effects: E_EffectMismatch
error: ...", "parser: E_RedundantBraces Warning: ...". That anchor cannot
match one, so the field printed 0 for all 148 micros on every gate run
since it was written. Measured on mn-payload, which reported diags=0 beside
an err file carrying thirteen diagnostic lines and a live E_EffectMismatch.
It counts ' error: ' now, and the battery sums the total and names the
fixtures carrying it, because a number nobody totals is a number nobody
reads.

The refuse contract matched only refuse:E_*. A fixture expecting a P_ / W_
/ T_ / V_ class fell through it to the value path, where its exit was
compared against the string refuse:P_UnclosedConstruct — not an integer
comparison, so the FAIL branch was never taken and the fixture passed while
asserting nothing. mn-string-newline expects refuse P_UnclosedConstruct and
had been reporting exit=42, green, for as long as it existed. It now passes
by refusing.

What this makes visible: 21 errors across 14 micros, in four classes —
15 E_EffectMismatch, 2 E_TypeMismatch, 2 E_ResumeOutsideArm, 2
E_PurityViolated. They are not new, only newly reported. Two of those
classes are armed, which is worth the next dig: an armed class should
refuse the executable, and these fixtures build and run.

Implement four Session-tentacle Interact handler arms in
mentl_voice_default. All four are pure handler-state operations —
biggest clean composition batch available without effect-extension
work (which Filesystem and Run arms require).

declare_intent(intent) — append (IntentId, Intent) tuple to handler
state's intents list (cons; most-recent-first); mint fresh IntentId
from next_intent_id counter; increment counter.

retract_intent(id) — remove the entry whose IntentId matches via
intents_without helper. Idempotent (no-op when id not present;
honest semantics for stale ids).

history(n) — return last n TurnRecords from handler state. If n
exceeds actual length, return full history. Most-recent at head
(per cons append in ask arm's prior_turn update).

cancel_pending() — reset prior_turn to None. Per Interact effect
comment 'rolls back a tentative application': pre-pending-edit
substrate (MV.2.e.P), the only tentative state is prior_turn;
clearing it gives surfaces a clean turn boundary when the user
invalidates a Mentl-initiated proposal.

Two helpers (Pure):
  intent_id_eq — IntentId destructure-and-compare
  intents_without — single-pass cons recursion (small N typical;
                    substrate idiom buf+counter reserved for large N)

mentl/3da8d79:
The B.4 multi-shot quartet's race combinator. Per HC2 walkthrough §6.1:
parallel speculation across N candidate MultiShot handlers on one
shared graph; one shared checkpoint at install; per-fork exploration;
deterministic tiebreak chain over verified survivors; trail rollback
of losers.

`race` is library-level — no new primitive. Composes graph + handlers
+ row + MS + Reason from existing substrate (primitives 1, 2, 4, 8).

Substrate landings:

- fn race(handlers) with GraphRead + GraphWrite — the public API.
  Wraps race_internal; consumers install via `~> race(h1, h2, h3)`.
- fn race_internal — the handler factory. Per Q-B.4.2: shared
  graph_push_checkpoint at install; collect_verified_survivors forks
  each input as MultiShot resume; first_verified_wins picks via
  tiebreak; graph_rollback to shared checkpoint; replay_winner
  re-applies the winner's mutations.
- fn collect_verified_survivors — caps forks at 8 per MO §2 (one fork
  per Mentl tentacle as the natural concurrency budget); filters by
  Verify discharge (only proven candidates survive).

Tiebreak chain (per QA Q-B.4.1 — DETERMINISTIC, no wall-clock):
- tiebreak_row_minimality — fewer effects in row wins
- tiebreak_reason_depth — shorter Reason chain wins (simpler proof)
- tiebreak_declared_intent — survivors aligned with user's Intent win
- tiebreak_source_span — earlier source position wins
- tiebreak_lex — alphabetic name; guarantees singleton

first_verified_wins composes the five steps via `|>` pipe chain;
last step's lex tiebreak guarantees a singleton output.
